extraction_notes: Fig. 1, Fig. 2, and Fig. 3 contain usable vector plots. Forward, reverse, and junction-capacitance points were directly digitized from the supplied plots; no intermediate points were synthesized. Fig. 4 power-derating vertices were transcribed directly from the plotted line.
Fig. 1 shows typical instantaneous forward characteristics at Ta = 25 degC and Ta = 100 degC. Forward-current values use the plotted A axis.
Fig. 2 shows typical reverse-current magnitude at Ta = 25 degC and Ta = 100 degC. Reverse-current values are represented as positive magnitudes and normalized from the plotted mA axis to A.

Fig. 3 shows typical junction capacitance between terminals at Ta = 25 degC and f = 1 MHz. Capacitance values are normalized from the plotted pF axis to F. The table separately specifies CT = 170 pF at VR = 0 V and f = 1 MHz.

Electrical-characteristics table maximum forward-voltage evidence for B0540WS is VF2 = 0.51 V at IF = 0.5 A and VF3 = 0.62 V at IF = 1.0 A, both at Ta = 25 degC. The separate VF1 row is blank for B0540WS.

Electrical-characteristics table maximum reverse-current evidence for B0540WS is IR = 0.01 mA at VR = 20 V and IR = 0.02 mA at VR = 40 V, at Ta = 25 degC. The rated DC blocking voltage is 40 V, so the 40 V row is used as the reverse-current fit target.

Absolute-rating bounds for B0540WS at Ta = 25 degC are VRRM = 40 V, VRMS = 28 V, VDC = 40 V, IF(AV) = 0.5 A, and IFSM = 5.5 A at t = 8.3 ms half-sine wave. Power dissipation is 200 mW, junction temperature is -55 to +125 degC, storage temperature is -55 to +150 degC, and typical RthetaJA is 500 degC/W.
The datasheet publishes no reverse-recovery-time, breakdown-voltage, or breakdown-current specification; VRRM and VDC ratings are operating limits, not breakdown data.
